cases.reason: The 2002 format has a WITH DEBUGGING MODE clause (obsolete in 2002) that the pointer's format lacks, so the pointer's evidence does not show it; and the PDF render (p212) shows the clause is its OWN optional bracket, not subordinate to computer-name-1 as in 1985 ('SOURCE-COMPUTER. [computer-name [WITH DEBUGGING MODE] .]'). SR1 confirms it ('neither computer-name-1 nor the DEBUGGING MODE clause'). The grammar keeps the 1985 shape at every edition: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:563 `sourceComputerParagraph : SOURCE_COMPUTER DOT (computerName debuggingModeClause? unrecognizedClause?)? DOT?`, so a name-less DEBUGGING MODE is a parse error at 2002 (COBOL1971). The named form works at 2002 with the obsolete warning. DebuggingLineRewriter.DeclaresMode scans tokens after the header and would already see a name-less clause; the fix is the grammar (edition-split: 1985 keeps the name requirement, 2002 does not; removed at 2014 per debugging-mode-removed-2014).
cases.needs: a fix and a 2002 witness: at --std 2002 `SOURCE-COMPUTER. WITH DEBUGGING MODE.` must be accepted (obsolete warning) and make debugging lines source; plus a 2002 witness for the named form (probe dbgon.cob: START/DEBUG-LINE/X=2)
